traceability.evidence:
Key implementation and test artifacts:
1) ESLint rule implementation - File: src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts - Declares the `require-branch-annotation` rule with full ESLint metadata: - `meta.type = "problem"`, `fixable = "code"`, schema with `branchTypes` option. - `docs.description: "Require @story and @req annotations on code branches"`. - JSDoc links directly to this story: - `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` - `@req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION` and `@req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE`. - `create(context)`: - Calls `validateBranchTypes(context)` (from branch-annotation-helpers) to resolve which branch node types to enforce (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE). - For each branch type returns a handler that: - Skips `SwitchCase` nodes that represent `default` (`test == null`), reflecting significance criteria. - Calls `reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef)`, which performs annotation detection and reporting (REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION, REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING). - Error message: - `missingAnnotation: "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}."` – a clear, parameterized message that matches the story’s user-experience goal.
2) Branch helper logic (detection, comment association, parsing, config, performance) - File: src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts - `DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES` (REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA): - Includes: `IfStatement`, `SwitchCase`, `TryStatement`, `CatchClause`, `ForStatement`, `ForOfStatement`, `ForInStatement`, `WhileStatement`, `DoWhileStatement`. - JSDoc references this story and REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA. - `validateBranchTypes(context)` (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE): - Reads `context.options[0].branchTypes`. - If `branchTypes` is an array: - Filters against DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES. - On invalid values returns a listener `{ Program: ProgramHandler }` which reports each invalid type with: - `message: Value "${t}" should be equal to one of the allowed values: ${DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES.join(", ")}`. - Otherwise returns the validated branchTypes. - If no `branchTypes` option present, returns DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES. - `gatherBranchCommentText(sourceCode, node)` (REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION): - Special-cases `SwitchCase` to scan up a few lines and collect preceding `//` or `/* */` comments, even through a blank line. - For other branch types, uses `sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node)` and maps comment nodes to their `.value` text. - Returns concatenated comment text associated with that branch. - `reportMissingStory` and `reportMissingReq` (REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING & UX): - Use `context.report` with `messageId: "missingAnnotation"` and `data: { missing: "@story" | "@req" }`. - Provide autofixes: - Inserts `// @story .story.md` or `// @req ` at the appropriate indentation and position above the branch. - `storyFixCountRef` ensures only the first missing `@story` gets an autofix, subsequent ones still error but without fix, controlling auto-fix scope. - `getBranchAnnotationInfo(...)` and `reportMissingAnnotations(...)`: - Extract combined comment text via `gatherBranchCommentText` and compute `missingStory` / `missingReq` using regex. - Determine insertion indentation and location via `sourceCode.lines` and `getIndexFromLoc`. - Build an `actions` array for story and req, and for each where `missing` is true, invokes the appropriate reporter. - This design is linear in the number of branch nodes and uses simple string operations, satisfying REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION for large files.
3) Rule tests mapped to this story - File: tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts - Header: - `Tests for: docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md, docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md`. - `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`. - `@req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION` plus error/reporting-related reqs. - Uses `RuleTester` to run the rule across many valid and invalid cases. - Valid cases (Core Functionality + Comment Association): - `if (condition) {}` with preceding `@story` + `@req` comments. - `for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {}` with block comments. - `switch (value)` with annotated `case 'a'` (both leading and inline variations). - `try`/`finally` and `try`/`catch` branches with annotations. - `do { ... } while (condition);`, `for..of`, `for..in`, `while (condition)` all with annotations. - Switch default case allowed without annotations to illustrate significance criteria. - Configurable scope: - With `options: [{ branchTypes: ["IfStatement"] }]`, a `switch` without annotations is valid. - With `options: [{ branchTypes: ["IfStatement", "SwitchCase"] }]`, an annotated `if` is valid and proves enforcement scope. - Invalid cases (Core Functionality + UX + Error Handling): - Missing annotations on each branch type: `if`, `for`, `while (true)`, `switch case` (including a version with a blank line before the case), `do-while`, `for-of`, `for-in`, `try` and `catch` blocks. - Each invalid case defines `errors` expecting an array of `missingAnnotation` messages with appropriate `data.missing` values. - Each invalid case specifies `output` that matches expected autofixed code, including inserted `// @story .story.md` and `// @req ` with correct indentation. - Configuration error scenario: - `options: [{ branchTypes: ["UnknownType"] }]` with a simple `if` body. - Expects an error whose message matches `/should be equal to one of the allowed values/`, verifying invalid configuration reporting behavior.
4) Helper tests - File: tests/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.test.ts - Header: - `Tests for: docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` and `@req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE`. - Tests `validateBranchTypes` specifically: - No options -> returns `DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES`. - Valid `branchTypes` -> returns exactly the provided list. - Invalid `branchTypes`: - Returns an object with a `Program` listener. - Invoking `Program(fakeNode)` results in `context.report` being called once per invalid type with messages containing `Value "" should be equal to one of the allowed values: ...`.
5) Plugin integration - File: src/index.ts - RULE_NAMES includes `"require-branch-annotation"`, so it is dynamically loaded. - `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES` maps `"traceability/require-branch-annotation"` to severity `"error"`. - `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict` are built from these severities and exported, meaning this rule is part of the core presets as the story’s Definition of Done requires. - Confirmed by passing tests in `tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts` (from the earlier `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose` run).
6) Rule documentation - File: docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md - References the story and requirements: - `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`. - `@req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION`, `@req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE`. - Explains: - What the rule does: enforces `@story` and `@req` on significant branches (if/else, switch, loops, try/catch). - `branchTypes` option, supported values, defaults, and behavior on invalid types. - Provides correct and incorrect code samples and an invalid configuration example, matching the implemented behavior.
7) Test execution evidence - Command executed (as required): - `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose`. - Jest output shows: - `PASS tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts` with all described valid/invalid tests passing. - `PASS tests/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.test.ts` confirming configuration behavior. - No failing suites or tests.
8) Alignment with acceptance criteria - **Core Functionality**: The rule detects missing `@story`/`@req` on all configured significant branches; verified by comprehensive invalid tests for all targeted AST node types. - **Quality Standards**: The rule follows ESLint best practices (meta, schema, RuleTester, small helpers) and uses efficient algorithms. - **Integration**: Works across multiple branch shapes, including try/catch/finally and loops; nested branches are inherently supported by AST traversal, and the rule is integrated into recommended and strict plugin presets. - **User Experience**: Clear, consistent error messages and helpful autofixes that insert placeholder annotations where appropriate. - **Error Handling**: Invalid configurations (unsupported branchTypes) are gracefully reported via a Program listener; edge cases like switch cases with preceding blank lines and switch defaults have explicit logic and tests. - **Documentation**: A dedicated rule document describes behavior, configuration, and examples, directly linked to this story.
No gaps were found between the story’s requirements and the implemented/tested behavior.
